name: default
note: Eight rules chosen for confidence rather than coverage. A rule that fires on a busy but healthy host teaches the analyst to ignore its whole category, so a signal earns a place here only when it is rare in normal operation or is qualified by a second, independent one.

rules.title: Injected process has external network activity
rules.note: A malfind region alone is common enough to be noise. The same region in a process talking to a routable address is the shape of a live implant.

rules.title: Suspicious thread executing in unbacked memory
rules.note: A thread whose start address lies outside any mapped module, in a process that also has executable private memory, is code that was written and then run.

rules.title: Running process absent from the active process list
rules.note: Recovered by pool scan, missing from the linked list, and carrying no exit time. The exit-time clause is what separates this from every process that has simply terminated.

rules.title: Possible process hollowing
rules.note: The mapped image does not match the file it claims to come from.

rules.title: Possible process ghosting
rules.note: The image file was marked for deletion before the section was mapped, so there is no file on disk to examine. The memory is the only copy.

rules.title: Process visible to one enumeration method but not another
rules.note: Cross-view discrepancy reported by PsXView. Kept alongside PROC-HIDDEN deliberately: the two derive the same conclusion by different routes, and disagreement between them is itself worth reading.

rules.title: Several independent anomalies on one process
rules.note: No single signal here is conclusive. Three at once on the same process is not a coincidence worth explaining away.

rules.title: Executable memory not backed by a file
rules.note: Malfind on its own. Every JIT compiler on the host produces this, so it is listed for completeness rather than escalated. The higher-severity rules above are the ones that qualify it.
